concepts.name: Antiderivative as reverse differentiation
concepts.summary: Recognise that an antiderivative of f is a function F whose derivative is f, and recall that it is not unique.

concepts.name: Indefinite integral and constant
concepts.summary: Explain that the indefinite integral represents a whole family of antiderivatives differing by a constant C.

concepts.name: Basic power rule for integrals
concepts.summary: Understand and state that the integral of x^n is x^(n+1)/(n+1) + C for n not equal to -1, and why n = -1 is excluded.

concepts.name: Area under a curve idea
concepts.summary: Explain that a definite integral measures signed area between a curve and the x-axis, with area below the axis counting negative.

concepts.name: Linearity of integration
concepts.summary: Understand that integrals split over sums and pull out constant factors, so terms can be integrated one at a time.

concepts.name: Standard integral formulas
concepts.summary: Recall antiderivatives of sin x, cos x, e^x, 1/x and sec^2 x by reversing known derivative rules.

misconceptions.text: The integral of 1/x is x^0/0 by the power rule, or is simply ln x with no absolute value needed.
The constant C can be dropped because it does not affect the answer.
A definite integral always gives a positive area.

concepts.name: Riemann sums
concepts.summary: Compute left, right and midpoint sums over a partition to approximate the area under a curve.

concepts.name: Definite integral as limit
concepts.summary: Interpret the definite integral as the limit of Riemann sums as the partition width goes to zero.

concepts.name: Properties of definite integrals
concepts.summary: Apply rules such as reversing limits, splitting intervals and comparison to evaluate and simplify definite integrals.

concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem evaluation
concepts.summary: Evaluate a definite integral as F(b) - F(a) using an antiderivative.

concepts.name: Accumulation function derivative
concepts.summary: Apply the fact that d/dx of the integral from a to x of f(t) dt equals f(x), including with a variable upper limit via the chain rule.

concepts.name: Basic u-substitution
concepts.summary: Choose u so that an inner function and its derivative appear, and integrate in terms of u.

concepts.name: Net change interpretation
concepts.summary: Use the integral of a rate of change to find net change such as displacement from velocity.

misconceptions.text: A Riemann sum gives the exact area for any number of rectangles.
When using u-substitution on a definite integral, the original x-limits can be kept after changing to u.
The integral of velocity gives total distance travelled rather than net displacement.

concepts.name: Integration by parts
concepts.summary: Apply the formula integral u dv = uv - integral v du, choosing u and dv sensibly, including repeated use and cyclic cases.

concepts.name: Trigonometric integrals
concepts.summary: Integrate products and powers of trig functions using identities and substitution.

concepts.name: Partial fraction decomposition
concepts.summary: Decompose a rational function into simpler fractions with linear and repeated factors and integrate each term.

concepts.name: Trigonometric substitution
concepts.summary: Select a sine, tangent or secant substitution based on the radical form and convert back to x using a reference triangle.

concepts.name: Area between curves
concepts.summary: Set up integrals for regions between curves by identifying intersections, upper and lower functions, and when to integrate in y.

concepts.name: Volumes by disks and washers
concepts.summary: Analyse a region and axis of rotation to build a disk or washer integral for the volume.

concepts.name: Method selection for integrals
concepts.summary: Analyse an integrand's form to decide among substitution, parts, partial fractions and trig substitution.

misconceptions.text: The integral of a product is the product of the integrals.
Partial fractions can be applied directly to any rational function, even when the numerator degree is at least the denominator degree.
Area between curves is always the integral of the right-hand function minus the left-hand function, regardless of which is on top.

concepts.name: Shell method
concepts.summary: Derive and apply shell integrals for volumes of revolution and compare when shells or washers give a simpler setup.

concepts.name: Arc length and surface area
concepts.summary: Set up arc length integrals using the square root of 1 + (f')^2 and extend to surface area of revolution.

concepts.name: Improper integrals
concepts.summary: Evaluate integrals with infinite limits or discontinuities by taking limits and decide convergence or divergence.

concepts.name: Comparison tests for improper integrals
concepts.summary: Judge convergence of an integral without computing it by comparing with p-integrals and other known cases.

concepts.name: Sequences and series convergence
concepts.summary: Distinguish convergence of a sequence from convergence of a series through its partial sums, using geometric and p-series as benchmarks.

concepts.name: Divergence and integral tests
concepts.summary: Apply the nth-term test and the integral test, checking its positivity, continuity and decreasing conditions.

concepts.name: Comparison and ratio tests
concepts.summary: Evaluate which of comparison, limit comparison, ratio or root tests suits a series and justify the conclusion.

concepts.name: Alternating series and absolute convergence
concepts.summary: Assess alternating series with the alternating series test and classify them as absolutely or conditionally convergent.

misconceptions.text: If the terms of a series tend to zero, the series must converge.
An integral from -infinity to infinity of an odd function is automatically zero.
The ratio test being inconclusive (limit equal to 1) means the series diverges.

concepts.name: Rigour of Riemann integrability
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a function is Riemann integrable using upper and lower sums, and recognise that continuous or bounded functions with finitely many discontinuities qualify.

concepts.name: Proof of the Fundamental Theorem
concepts.summary: Critique and reconstruct the proof linking differentiation and integration via the mean value theorem for integrals.

concepts.name: Numerical integration error analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate trapezoidal and Simpson's rules by deriving or applying error bounds and choosing step size for a target accuracy.

concepts.name: Integrals without elementary antiderivatives
concepts.summary: Judge when an integral such as e^(-x^2) has no closed form and select series or numerical approaches instead.

concepts.name: Power series integration
concepts.summary: Construct power series for integrands and integrate term by term within the radius of convergence to obtain series for functions and values.

concepts.name: Taylor remainder and error bounds
concepts.summary: Evaluate approximation accuracy using Taylor remainder and alternating series bounds to justify a truncation.

concepts.name: Modelling with integrals
concepts.summary: Design integral models for quantities such as work, mass, probability, centroids or fluid force by slicing and accumulating.

misconceptions.text: Every continuous function has an antiderivative expressible in elementary functions.
Term-by-term integration of a power series is valid on any interval, even outside the radius of convergence.
Simpson's rule is always more accurate than the trapezoid rule regardless of the function's smoothness.
